source_text: Est ebrietas sanctorum — spiritu non vino. Apostoli putabantur musto pleni. Discerne calices.
orientation: Origen is explaining that the priests' prohibition of wine points to a spiritual sobriety, and he now contrasts worldly drunkenness with the holy intoxication of the Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: Is drunkenness [of the] saints — [by the] spirit not [by] wine. [The] apostles were thought [with] new wine full. Distinguish [the] cups.

lemmas.gloss: of the holy ones, of the saints

choices.why: Keeps the paradoxical noun phrase as a single idea, preserving the rhetorical contrast with ordinary drunkenness.

choices.english: by the Spirit, not by wine
choices.why: The ablatives of means are rendered with 'by' to show the instrument of each state, keeping the sharp antithesis.
rejected: with the Spirit not with wine

choices.why: Mustum is specifically new or sweet wine, and 'full of' preserves the predicate adjective construction.
The imperative is kept as a direct command, and 'cups' preserves the concrete image of different drinks.

pass_b_english: There is a drunkenness of the saints—by the Spirit, not by wine. The apostles were thought to be full of new wine (Acts 2:13). Distinguish the cups.
